title: Longest Harmonious Subsequence

concept.title: Neighbouring values, counted together
body: A **harmonious** subsequence is one in which the largest value minus the smallest value is exactly 1. You may pick elements from anywhere (a subsequence does not have to be contiguous, and the order does not matter for the length). So such a subsequence uses only two values `x` and `x + 1`, and you can take **all** copies of both.
Both values must be present: with only one value the difference would be 0, not 1. A hash map of counts answers "is `x + 1` present and how often?" for every value in O(1).

statement: Choose some elements of an array (not necessarily next to each other) so that the difference between the largest and the smallest chosen value is exactly 1. Print the largest number of elements you can choose, or 0 if no two values differ by exactly 1.
outputFormat: Print the largest number of elements.

examples.note: Take 3, 2, 2, 2, 3: five elements with values 2 and 3.

hints: The chosen values must be x and x + 1 for some x.
You can take all copies of both values.
Count the values and check every x for which x + 1 is present.
